evidence.support_text: Exposure of reconstructed human epidermis containing LC-like cells to the skin sensitiser nickel(II) sulfate (NiSO₄) induced a reduction in the number of LC-like cells and affected their dendritic morphology (fewer and shorter dendrites), as reported in paragraph 63.

evidence.support_text: Hapten (picryl chloride)-modified LC-enriched EC populations were found also to induce specific proliferative responses by lymphocytes prepared from mice treated with the same chemical.

evidence.assay_type: subcutaneous injection of hapten-derivatized Ia+ epidermal cells
evidence.experimental_conditions: high concentrations of DNFB, in vitro derivatization of Ia+-enriched epidermal cells, subcutaneous injection into naive mice
evidence.support_text: By contrast, similar epidermal cell suspensions derivatized with high concentrations of DNFB neither induced CH in naive mice.

evidence.assay_type: subcutaneous injection of hapten-derivatized Ia+ epidermal cells
evidence.experimental_conditions: low concentrations of DNFB, in vitro derivatization of Ia+-enriched epidermal cells (Langerhans cells), subcutaneous injection into naive mice
evidence.support_text: Dai and Streilein [8] reported that epidermal cell suspensions enriched for Ia+ cells, then derivatized in vitro with low concentrations of DNFB induced CH when injected subcutaneously into naive mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: in vitro, Langerhans cells as antigen-presenting cells, class II-binding lysine-containing peptides photomodified with ofloxacin, CD4+ T cells from sensitized BALB/c mice
evidence.support_text: CD4⁺ T cells were purified from lymph nodes of BALB/c mice sensitized subcutaneously with ofloxacin-photomodified epidermal cells and from those sensitized epicutaneously via barrier-disrupted skin with a major histocompatibility complex class II (I-A<sup>d</sup>)-binding, ofloxacin-photoconjugated peptide. These immune T cells proliferated in vitro in response to Langerhans cells loaded with class II-binding, lysine-containing peptides when photomodified with ofloxacin.

evidence.assay_type: T cell proliferation assay using LC-enriched epidermal cells
evidence.experimental_conditions: LC-enriched epidermal cells prepared from FLRX/UVA-treated mice co-cultured with sensitized T cells from FLRX-photoallergic mice.
evidence.support_text: LC-enriched epidermal cells prepared from FLRX/UVA-treated mice induced the proliferation of sensitized T cells, indicating that photomodified Langerhans cells are functional in presenting photoantigen.

evidence.experimental_conditions: topical application, human skin
evidence.support_text: DNTB was associated with a decrease in the free thiol layer in the stratum corneum, but not in the nucleated epidermis.

evidence.assay_type: Ultrastructural evaluation of Langerhans cell activation
evidence.experimental_conditions: Subtoxic dose 0.25% DNCB, time points 1 to 96 h after application, high responder guinea pig strain
evidence.support_text: Activation of the LCs was most pronounced in animals treated with subtoxic 0.25% DNCB. First alterations were already present 1 h after application, increased after 6 and 24 h, and lasted up to 96 h. This indicates that DNCB treatment resulted in LC activation as measured by ultrastructural changes.

evidence.assay_type: Ultrastructural evaluation of Langerhans cell activation
evidence.experimental_conditions: Toxic dose: 3% DCP, time point not specified, high responder guinea pig strain
evidence.support_text: After skin painting with toxic 1% and 10% DNCB, 5% Ox, and 3% DCP, the LC activation was paralleled by some degenerative alterations such as cytoplasmic edema, mitochondrial swelling, and irregular endoplasmic vacuolization. Thus, DCP at 3% also caused LC activation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4.4 × 10^7 mesenteric lymph node cells from TNCB-fed donor mice (5 days post-feeding) injected iv into naive C57BL/6 mice; ear challenged with TNCB; ear thickness measured 24 h later
evidence.support_text: In Experiment 2, 4.4 × 10^7 mesenteric lymph node cells from TNCB-fed mice (5 days after feeding) were injected iv into naive mice, which were then challenged on the ear with TNCB. The increase in ear thickness at 24 hr was 12.9 ± 1.2 × 10^-4 in. (mean ± SD), indicating positive contact sensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4.5×10^7 mesenteric lymph node cells from TNCB-fed donor mice (5 days post-feeding) injected iv into naive C57BL/6 mice; ear challenged with TNCB; ear thickness measured 24 h later
evidence.support_text: In Experiment 1, 4.5 × 10^7 mesenteric lymph node cells from TNCB-fed mice (5 days after feeding) were injected iv into naive mice, which were then challenged on the ear with TNCB. The increase in ear thickness at 24 hr was 9.8 ± 1.0 × 10^-4 in. (mean ± SD), indicating positive contact sensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 6 × 10^7 splenic cells from TNCB-fed donor mice (5 days post-feeding) injected iv into naive C57BL/6 mice; ear challenged with TNCB; ear thickness measured 24 h later
evidence.support_text: In Experiment 1, 6 × 10^7 splenic cells from TNCB-fed mice (5 days after feeding) were injected iv into naive mice, which were then challenged on the ear with TNCB. The increase in ear thickness at 24 hr was 8.5 ± 0.9 × 10^-4 in. (mean ± SD), indicating positive contact sensitivity.

evidence.support_text: In Experiment 2, 6 × 10^7 splenic cells from TNCB-fed mice (5 days after feeding) were injected iv into naive mice, which were then challenged on the ear with TNCB. The increase in ear thickness at 24 hr was 11.1 ± 1.3 × 10^-4 in. (mean ± SD), indicating positive contact sensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Naive T cells activated by DNFB-derivatized cEC or cSAC were injected into ear skin of naive mice; challenge with 40 µg DNFB painted on ear.
evidence.support_text: Naive T cells activated by DNFB-derivatized cultured EC or SAC induced vigorous contact hypersensitivity when injected into ear skin of naive mice followed by challenge with 40 µg DNFB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Donor mice fed TNCB in olive oil 5 days before; 4.5e7 mesenteric lymph node cells transferred iv to naive recipients; immediate ear challenge with TNCB; ear swelling measured 24 hr later.
evidence.support_text: Experiment 1: 4.5 x 10^7 mesenteric lymph node cells obtained 5 days after feeding TNCB were injected iv into naive mice; recipients were challenged on the ear with TNCB and CS measured 24 hr later. The increase in ear thickness was 9.8 (1.0) x 10^-4 in, compared to 2.6 (0.8) for negative controls.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Donor mice fed TNCB in olive oil 5 days before; 4.5e7 spleen cells transferred iv to naive recipients; immediate ear challenge with TNCB; ear swelling measured 24 hr later.
evidence.support_text: Experiment 1: 4.5 x 10^7 splenic cells obtained 5 days after feeding TNCB were injected iv into naive mice; recipients were challenged on the ear with TNCB and CS measured 24 hr later. The increase in ear thickness was 8.5 (0.9) x 10^-4 in.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Donor mice fed TNCB in olive oil 5 days before; cells (mixture of intraepithelial and lamina propria lymphocytes) transferred iv to naive recipients; immediate ear challenge with TNCB; ear swelling measured 24 hr later.
evidence.support_text: Lymphoid cells from ... a mixture of intraepithelial and lamina propria lymphocytes (IEL + LPL) obtained 5 days after feeding TNCB were injected iv into normal mice. Significant CS was transferred to normal mice with lymphoid cells from mesenteric lymph nodes, IEL + LPL and spleen, but not by those from PP.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Donor mice fed TNCB in olive oil 5 days before; Peyer's patch cells transferred iv to naive recipients; immediate ear challenge with TNCB; ear swelling measured 24 hr later.
evidence.support_text: Significant CS was transferred to normal mice with lymphoid cells from mesenteric lymph nodes, IEL + LPL and spleen, but not by those from PP.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cells from TNCB-fed mice (day 5) transferred to naive mice; cells treated with anti-Thy1.2 and anti-Lyt1.1 antibodies plus complement to identify T lymphocytes
evidence.support_text: Cells from gut-associated lymphoid tissues and spleen of TNCB-fed mice were able to adoptively transfer CS to naive mice; this capacity was abrogated after treating cells with anti-Thy1.2 and anti-Lyt1.1 antibodies plus complement, identifying the effector cells as T lymphocytes (p:0).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application to skin of C3H/HeN mice, contact sensitization protocol; CHS did not occur in C57BL/6 mice.
evidence.support_text: Application of DMBA to the skin of C3H/HeN mice resulted in antigen-specific contact hypersensitivity (CHS) to that agent. In CD8 knockout mice, CHS to DMBA was reduced compared to wildtype, while in CD4 knockout mice the response was exaggerated, indicating that CD8+ T-cells are predominant effectors and CD4+ T-cells have a regulatory role in DMBA CHS.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 125 µg DNFB epicutaneous sensitization on day 0; 5 days later, 40 µg DNFB challenge on ear in BALB/c mice
evidence.support_text: BALB/c mice received 125 µg DNFB epicutaneously; 5 days later, ears were injected with saline (control) or TNFα and then challenged with 40 µg DNFB. The CH response of the TNFα-treated panel was significantly increased compared with saline-injected controls, indicating that DNFB alone induced a contact hypersensitivity response in the control group.

evidence.assay_type: contact hypersensitivity (CH) induction via dermal grafts
evidence.experimental_conditions: epicutaneous application of conventional (suprathreshold) doses of DNFB to syngeneic skin, then dermal grafts from painted skin transferred to naive mice
evidence.support_text: Bacci et al. [3] demonstrated that CH was induced in mice that received dermal, but not epidermal, grafts prepared from syngeneic skin painted epicutaneously with conventional doses of DNFB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.2% DNFB; sensitization on abdomen; challenge on ears; mouse strain: C57Bl/6; vehicle not specified
evidence.support_text: WT and Bid KO mice were sensitized on the abdomen and challenged on ears with 0.2% dinitrofluorobenzene (DNFB). Ear swelling responses were accelerated in Bid KO mice and enhanced 2.3-fold over WT mouse responses, indicating that DNFB induces a contact hypersensitivity response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: DMBA challenge; FVB control mice; measurement at 48 h; specific concentration not reported
evidence.support_text: FVB control mice challenged with the sensitizing agent DMBA showed ear swelling of 2.8 ± 0.4 ×10⁻³ inches at 48 h.

evidence.experimental_conditions: DMBA challenge; FVB-DKO mice; measurement at 48 h; specific concentration not reported
evidence.support_text: FVB-DKO mice demonstrated similar increased ear swelling to the sensitizing agent DMBA (5.8 ± 0.7 vs 2.8 ± 0.4 in controls; p < 0.0002).

evidence.experimental_conditions: monobenzone-induced CHS in mice
evidence.support_text: Van Den Boorn et al. reported that monobenzone (a pro-hapten) stimulated NLRP3 inflammasome activation to induce adaptive NK cell memory and contact hypersensitivity (CHS), whereas the absence of the NLRP3 inflammasome, ASC or interleukin-18 abolished monobenzone-induced CHS.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Sensitization and challenge with TNCB in mice; specific protocol details not reported
evidence.support_text: Mice sensitized and challenged with TNCB exhibited ear swelling responses; these responses were reduced by 80% in TNF-/-, TNFR1-/-, and W/Wv mice, demonstrating a positive CHSR in wild-type mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: trinitrophenylchloride-induced CHS in wild-type mice
evidence.support_text: Sutterwala et al. showed that in a trinitrophenylchloride-induced contact hypersensitivity (CHS) model, NLRP3 and ASC-deficient mice had an impaired CHS response compared with wild-type mice, indicating that trinitrophenylchloride induces CHS in wild-type mice.

evidence.assay_type: Contact hypersensitivity (CHS) assay in UVB-irradiated mice
evidence.experimental_conditions: C3H/HeN mice fed GSPs-supplemented diet or control diet, exposed to UVB radiation, sensitized with DNFB; ear swelling measured after challenge.
evidence.support_text: Dietary supplementation with grape seed proanthocyanidins (GSPs) resulted in enhancement of immune sensitivity or contact hypersensitivity (CHS) responses in UVB-exposed C3H/HeN mice. The CHS response was measured following sensitization and challenge with DNFB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: FITC-sensitized mouse; topical application of FITC and Pam2Cys during challenge; unspecified concentration and vehicle.
evidence.support_text: In FITC-sensitized mice, topical application of Pam2Cys together with FITC during challenge significantly decreased FITC-specific IgE and IgG1 antibodies compared to mice receiving FITC alone.

evidence.experimental_conditions: FITC-sensitized mouse; topical application of FITC and Pam2Cys during challenge; unspecified concentration and vehicle.
evidence.support_text: In FITC-sensitized mice, topical application of Pam2Cys together with FITC during challenge significantly decreased FITC-specific T-cell proliferation compared to mice receiving FITC alone.

evidence.experimental_conditions: FITC-sensitized mouse; topical application of FITC and Pam2Cys during challenge; unspecified concentration and vehicle.
evidence.support_text: In FITC-sensitized mice, topical application of Pam2Cys together with FITC during challenge significantly reduced ear swelling by >80% compared to mice receiving FITC alone.

evidence.experimental_conditions: FITC-sensitized mouse; topical application of FITC and Pam3Cys during challenge; unspecified concentration and vehicle.
evidence.support_text: In FITC-sensitized mice, topical application of Pam3Cys together with FITC during challenge did not change the course of subsequently induced CHS inflammation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mice, allergen-induced CHS model (allergen unspecified)
evidence.support_text: The NOS inhibitor L-nitroarginine methyl ester (L-NAME) suppressed allergen-induced contact hypersensitivity (CHS) in mice, indicating that inhibition of NO synthesis reduces the skin sensitization response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: DNFB sensitization in Mas-TRECK Tg mice; comparison to wild-type
evidence.support_text: In Mas-TRECK Tg mice (mast cell depleted), DNFB-induced contact hypersensitivity was significantly attenuated, indicating that DNFB induces CHS in mice with normal mast cells.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse model, skin exposed to the compound
evidence.support_text: Mice reconstituted with RORγt cDNA-transduced haematopoietic stem cells showed attenuated severity of contact hypersensitivity on skin exposed to 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene, indicating that the compound induced contact hypersensitivity in this model.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse model; Nrf2-deficient vs wild-type mice
evidence.support_text: Exposure to the chemical sensitizer 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB) induced a more severe inflammatory response in Nrf2-deficient mice compared to wild-type mice, indicating DNCB's ability to induce contact hypersensitivity, a skin sensitization adverse outcome.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice treated with 3-methylcholanthrene to induce cytochrome P450
evidence.support_text: In contrast, no contact sensitization is generated by other alkaloids such as ... ephedrine ... probably because stimulation by 3-methylcholanthrene does not induce the appropriate cytochrome P450 isoenzymes.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice treated with 3-methylcholanthrene to induce cytochrome P450
evidence.support_text: In contrast, no contact sensitization is generated by other alkaloids such as ... nicotine ... probably because stimulation by 3-methylcholanthrene does not induce the appropriate cytochrome P450 isoenzymes.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice treated with 3-methylcholanthrene to induce cytochrome P450
evidence.support_text: In contrast, no contact sensitization is generated by other alkaloids such as atropine, ... probably because stimulation by 3-methylcholanthrene does not induce the appropriate cytochrome P450 isoenzymes.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice treated with 3-methylcholanthrene to induce cytochrome P450
evidence.support_text: In mice, monocrotaline is only sensitizing if the appropriate cytochrome P450 is stimulated by 3-methylcholanthrene.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice treated with piperonyl butoxide (P450 inhibitor)
evidence.support_text: Inhibition of this P450 by piperonyl butoxide completely abrogates the CHS reaction to monocrotaline (induction and elicitation).

evidence.experimental_conditions: applied to mouse skin; study in context of PDT-induced immunosuppression
evidence.support_text: PDT was initially discovered to be immunosuppressive in mice using dinitrofluorobenzene (DNFB), a sensitizing agent that induces a contact hypersensitivity response. In this study, mice treated with PDT showed a significant decrease in their cell-mediated immune response to DNFB applied to the PDT-treated area.

evidence.assay_type: contact hypersensitivity assay (occlusive chamber epicutaneous sensitization)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Epicutaneous application via occlusive chamber (1-2 cm diameter) for 6 hr; challenge with 1% TNCB on ear 5 days later; mouse strains BALB/c, C3H/HeN, C57BL/6; dose range 3.5-3500 µg, minimum sensitizing dose 35 µg for BALB/c.
evidence.support_text: Epicutaneous application of trinitrobenzene sulfonic acid (TNBS, 3500 µg) in an occlusive chamber for 6 hours to BALB/c, C3H/HeN, and C57BL/6 mice induced intense contact hypersensitivity when challenged 5 days later with 1% trinitrochlorobenzene (TNCB) on the ear. The minimum sensitizing dose was 35 µg for BALB/c mice, comparable to the epicutaneous sensitization dose of TNCB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse model, FITC sensitization and challenge; biphasic reaction observed – immediate IgE-mediated and delayed cell-mediated (24-48 h).
evidence.support_text: Using selective depletion and adoptive transfer techniques, it was found that the conventional (delayed) contact hypersensitivity reaction elicited in FITC sensitized mice was mediated only by Th2-type CD4 T lymphocytes.

evidence.assay_type: contact hypersensitivity induction in TLR knockout mice
evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse model with TLR2/TLR4 double deletion or TLR2/TLR4/IL-12Rβ2 deletions
evidence.support_text: In Toll-like receptor deletion mutants (ΔTLR2/ΔTLR4 or ΔTLR2 or 4/ΔIL-12Rβ2), mice could not be sensitised to 2,4,6-trinitro-1-chlorobenzene (TNCB), indicating that TLR signalling is required for sensitization.

evidence.assay_type: contact hypersensitivity induction in wild-type mice
evidence.experimental_conditions: wild-type mice, exposure to nickel alone
evidence.support_text: Mice do not develop contact hypersensitivity to nickel unless LPS is co-injected, because mouse TLR4 lacks the histidine residues that interact with nickel ions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: ICR mouse skin, PA treatment alone
evidence.support_text: Treatment of ICR mouse skin with protocatechuic acid alone resulted in tyrosinase-dependent contact hypersensitivity, a skin sensitization adverse outcome.

evidence.experimental_conditions: C3H/HEN female mice; intragastric administration of TNCB; challenge with hapten (epidermal); ear swelling measured
evidence.support_text: Contact sensitivity (CS) was found to be present 5 days after feeding TNCB, and the magnitude of reactivity in orally sensitized mice was somewhat less than that of epidermally sensitized mice (p:0).

evidence.experimental_conditions: DNFB as contact sensitizer; mouse model (in vivo ear swelling or similar); Nf1+/+ and Nf1+/- littermates
evidence.support_text: In vivo contact sensitivity studies using DNFB revealed increased cutaneous inflammation and mast cell degranulation in Nf1+/− versus +/+ littermates. This indicates that DNFB induces a skin sensitization response in mice, with enhanced response in Nf1 heterozygous mice.

evidence.assay_type: delayed-type hypersensitivity (footpad swelling) test in mice
evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse; footpad injection; maximal tolerated dose 24 mM; concentrations tested 2.4–24.4 mM; percent of paw weight swelling measured
evidence.support_text: When solutions of TCNQ and TTF in ethanol at concentrations of 12·2-24·4 mM were used, a clear increase in footpad swelling was noticed. A test substance concentration of 2·4 mM did not significantly change paw weight, and this dose was used as maximum tolerated. The data achieved after animal immunization indicate that there was not a clear increase in footpad swelling (Table 5). Thus, at concentrations of 2·4-24·4 mM, delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction was not enhanced by ethanolic solutions of TCNQ and TTF.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice, ethanol solution
evidence.support_text: Delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction in mice indicated that TCNQ used as an ethanol solution was not allergic.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse model; FITC-CHS protocol
evidence.support_text: Tributyrin had an adjuvant effect on FITC-induced contact hypersensitivity (FITC-CHS) during the sensitization phase in mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: BALB/c mice; topical application of FITC with phthalate esters; details in Imai et al., 2006
evidence.support_text: The paper states that DEHP did not enhance the sensitization to FITC or DC-trafficking (Imai et al., 2006), indicating a lack of adjuvant effect in the FITC model.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse model; skin sensitization with FITC in presence of dibutyrin isomer
evidence.support_text: Each dibutyrin isomer slightly enhanced skin sensitization to FITC in a mouse model of contact hypersensitivity.
